author: Rory Robinson
title: Lindsey Vonn opens up about depression battle after debilitating Winter Olympics accident - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
1 hours ago While Team USA skier Lindsey Vonn made her rehabilitation process appear to be full of support following her injury at the Winter Olympics in Italy, she admitted that her reality was lonelier and more depressing than it seemed.
Vonn's Winter Olympics crash that left her physically broken and mentally isolated during the women’s downhill event. A crash that forced her to be airlifted off the mountain left her immobile and alone in the hospital for two and a half weeks.
That stretch badly impacted her mental health as the Team USA star tried to process what had happened and how completely her life had changed. Family members and high-profile TV stars also visited Vonn in Italy during her recovery process.
Meanwhile, President Donald Trump continues to be slammed over "sexist" comments regarding women's athletes .

• New Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel photos cast doubt on NFL insider's line of defense
Speaking to PEOPLE , Vonn described her emotional state as “up and down” while battling depression and said the hardest part was being so dependent on others for basic needs. "I'd say in the last month, it's definitely gotten better, but of course there were really low moments," she said.
"It was quite a challenge, just being in the hospital alone for two and a half weeks," she continued. Being completely immobile for that extended time period was so rough."
A combination of being stuck in bed, cut off from normal life, and reading detractors' criticism online caused her to struggle. Vonn tried to avoid the harsh words initially, but not always successfully.
A vocal group of Olympic spectators questioned why Vonn would take a potential spot from a new prospect by rushing back to compete after she had ruptured her ACL just nine days prior. Some also indicated an opinion that Vonn overvalued the odds of requiring a leg amputation .
After changing her mind on retirement in 2024, Vonn qualified for Team USA through results after winning a World Cup downhill race in St. Moritz.
The Team USA star acknowledged that she occasionally responded to those online trolls without much regret and defended herself, perhaps too often, while feeling frustrated and vulnerable in the hospital.
In the weeks after the crash, Vonn also revealed that her dog Leo died one day later after a battle with lung cancer . Vonn also says the last month has been better and that she feels closer to getting her life back.
Vonn continues to recover from a shattered left leg and multiple surgeries , and the expectation of one more operation later this year. She remains on crutches and is expected to continue rehab with plans to be able to walk without assistance by May.
The Olympics marked Vonn's return to skiing after six years of inactivity, following a knee replacement in 2024 and a torn ACL sustained while training for the games.
